$description: Neutral layout defaults for content measure, gutters, gaps, grid, navigation size and shell arrangement. Layouts must redefine every one of these. The shell and the layout primitives (idg-stack, idg-cluster, idg-grid, idg-sidebar, idg-switcher, idg-cover) read them.

content-max.$description: Maximum inline size of the page content; 100% lets it run edge to edge.

page-gutter.$description: Inline padding between the page content and the viewport edge.

section-gap.$description: Block gap between the sections of a page.

gap.$description: Default gap inside the layout primitives; multiply by --idg-density-gap-scale to follow the UX mode.

columns.$description: Most columns idg-grid draws, however wide it is.

grid-min.$description: Default minimum track size of idg-grid.

aside-width.$description: Default width of the side region of idg-sidebar.

nav-size.$description: Thickness of the bar or strip across the top that carries the navigation or the page actions.

rail-width.$description: Width of a navigation rail, and of the drawer that replaces the navigation when it collapses.

sticky-inset.$description: Block size of chrome that stays pinned to the top of the viewport, so scrolling a focused element into view leaves it clear of that chrome; 0 when nothing is pinned.

shell.$description: Which of the eight arrangements idg-layout draws. Each layout names itself, so the shell can tell them apart with a style query.
